skill.name: reading-logseq-data
skill.description: Read Logseq graph data through the Logseq HTTP API or CLI. Use it to fetch pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, and Datalog query results.
skill.summary: Read Logseq pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, and Datalog query results.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: Most static detections in the Markdown and query templates are false positives from documentation backticks, error strings, and Logseq Datalog syntax. The implementation still has real security-sensitive behavior: configurable token-bearing HTTP requests, environment and config secret access, and one CLI subprocess path for user-provided queries. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Bearer tokens can be sent to a configurable API URL.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict the default client to loopback URLs, warn or require confirmation for non-loopback hosts, and document trusted endpoint requirements.

remediation.issue: Search text is interpolated directly into a Datalog string.
remediation.suggestion: Escape string values or rewrite the fallback search query to pass user text through Datalog parameters.

remediation.issue: The CLI fallback runs a PATH-resolved logseq executable.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve a trusted executable path, document the command, and require explicit user choice before CLI fallback runs.

remediation.issue: Project-local configuration can control token and graph access.
remediation.suggestion: Validate .claude/logseq-expert/env.json, reject unexpected keys, and avoid environment-variable indirection from untrusted workspaces.

semantic_findings.title: Configurable API Endpoint Receives Token
semantic_findings.description: The client loads the API URL and token from environment or local config, then sends a bearer token to self.url/api. A malicious or unsafe configuration could redirect Logseq credentials and query payloads to an unintended endpoint.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL, token loading, and Authorization header are explicit in the client. Exploitation depends on attacker control of environment or local config, so the risk is contextual.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Search Text In Datalog Query
semantic_findings.description: The fallback search query inserts query_text directly inside a quoted Datalog string. Crafted text containing quotes or query syntax could alter the generated query or expose more graph data than intended.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The f-string directly interpolates user search text into query syntax without escaping or parameters. The impact is limited to Logseq query behavior, not shell execution.

content.value_statement: Logseq graphs can be hard to inspect from an AI coding session. This skill provides guided read access for pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, search, and Datalog queries.
actual_capabilities: Fetches Logseq pages and blocks by title or UUID.
Runs Datalog queries against a Logseq graph.
Searches graph content and returns matching blocks.
Lists pages and retrieves backlink relationships.
Reads page and block properties from graph data.
Uses HTTP API access or a Logseq CLI fallback.
limitations: Requires a running Logseq API or an installed Logseq CLI.
Needs a valid token, graph path, or local configuration.
Only reads graph data and does not edit Logseq content.
CLI behavior can vary by Logseq version and local setup.

use_cases.title: Inspect Project Notes
use_cases.description: Fetch project pages, open related blocks, and summarize current notes without leaving the coding session.
use_cases.target_user: Developers using Logseq for technical planning

use_cases.title: Query Knowledge Graphs
use_cases.description: Run focused Datalog queries to find tagged items, properties, tasks, and relationships in a Logseq graph.

use_cases.title: Review Linked Context
use_cases.description: Find backlinks and references for a topic before drafting documentation or making product decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the Logseq page named Project Alpha and summarize the main points and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Search Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my Logseq graph for onboarding and list the most relevant pages with short context for each match.

prompt_templates.title: Review Backlinks
prompt_templates.prompt: Find backlinks for the Architecture page and group the results by source page and topic.

prompt_templates.title: Run Focused Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Datalog query for tasks marked In Progress with priority High, then summarize owners, due dates, and blockers.

output_examples.input: Read the page Meeting Notes and summarize the actions.
output_examples.output: A short summary of the page, followed by action items, owners, and linked follow-up pages.
A grouped backlink review showing source pages, matching block summaries, and relationship notes.

output_examples.input: Search for security review in my Logseq graph.
output_examples.output: A ranked list of matching pages and blocks with concise excerpts and suggested next reads.

best_practices: Use the narrowest page title, block UUID, or search phrase that answers the task.
Prefer parameterized Datalog queries when values come from user text.
Keep Logseq API tokens in local environment variables or trusted configuration only.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad graph-wide queries when a page or tag lookup is enough.
Do not share Logseq API tokens in prompts, logs, or public repositories.
Do not use a remote API URL unless you fully trust the endpoint.

faq.question: Does this skill write to my Logseq graph?
faq.answer: No. The documented operations are read focused and cover pages, blocks, properties, search, backlinks, and queries.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need the Logseq HTTP API with a token, or the Logseq CLI with access to your graph.

faq.question: Can it run custom Datalog queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Datalog query examples and a client method for running graph queries.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it search across all notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can search graph content and return matching blocks, subject to the configured backend.

faq.question: What security precautions should I take?
faq.answer: Use localhost when possible, protect your API token, and avoid untrusted configuration files.
